item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q016_pdb_1acc_domain_split","answer":"SCOP 1.75 represented PDB 1acc chain A as a single domain, d1acca_. Later SCOPe 2.x releases revised that chain into two domains, d1acca1 and d1acca2. Thus the old whole-chain assignment should not be treated as one indivisible evolutionary unit: the two regions are independently recognizable structural/evolutionary modules that have been combined in one protein architecture. For homology searches, search each revised domain separately using its own boundaries or profile. A match confined to one domain supports homology only for that module; it does not establish homology of the other domain, the complete chain, or the full multidomain architecture, and it does not by itself justify transferring whole-protein function. Whole-chain templates are appropriate only when the target also preserves both domains and their organization; otherwise domain-specific templates and local alignments should be used.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
